source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in LLMs
finding: Eight hand-written exemplars with steps before the answer lift PaLM 540B on math and reasoning; gain grows with problem difficulty.
limits: Founding result. Gain is largest where baseline is lowest; easy one-step tasks gain little.
agent_relevance: Steps help most on multi-step items. Do not force steps on easy items (G11).

source: Wei et al. (2022) CoT: scale analysis
finding: CoT is an emergent ability: it does not help, and often hurts, small models.
numbers: Text: gains only at about 100B parameters; small models write fluent but illogical chains. Appendix: LaMDA 420M-8B stay near zero on several sets.
quote: chain of thought actually hurts performance for most models smaller than 10B parameters
limits: 2022-era models only. Later small models trained on CoT data do gain.
agent_relevance: Scaffold gains depend on model strength; test per model.

source: Wei et al. (2022) CoT: ablations
finding: Three ablations on GSM8K (LaMDA 137B, PaLM 540B): equation only, dots for extra compute, steps after the answer. Only natural-language steps before the answer give the full gain.
numbers: Variable-compute (dots) about equal to baseline; CoT-after-answer about equal to baseline; equation-only helps on easy sets but not GSM8K.
quote: Variable compute by itself is not the reason for the success of chain-of-thought prompting
limits: Ablation covers few datasets and two model families.
agent_relevance: Order matters: reasoning must come before the answer. Extra tokens alone do nothing.

source: Wei et al. (2022) CoT: symbolic tasks
finding: Symbolic tasks go from near chance to near ceiling for the largest model, with partial length generalisation.
numbers: Appendix Table 6/7 rows for PaLM 540B show standard 49.3 -> CoT 98.6 and standard 54.8 -> CoT 90.2 on two symbolic columns (column labels garbled in text extraction); 8B PaLM only 47.3 -> 57.1 and 50.9 -> 51.8.
limits: Exemplars written by authors; synthetic tasks.
agent_relevance: Length generalisation is partial; keep tasks near exemplar form.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large language models are zero-shot reasoners
finding: The phrase 'Let's think step by step' gives much of the CoT gain with no exemplars.
numbers: text-davinci-002: MultiArith 17.7 -> 78.7; GSM8K 10.4 -> 40.7 (zero-shot vs zero-shot-CoT). Few-shot-CoT reaches 93.0 on MultiArith in the same table.
limits: Little gain on commonsense tasks; exemplars still beat the trigger.
agent_relevance: A cheap trigger exists; exemplars give more.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) trigger-phrase sensitivity
finding: Different trigger sentences gave very different MultiArith scores.
numbers: Best instructive prompt 78.7 on MultiArith vs 17.7 baseline.
limits: Single model and dataset.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording is a free parameter; do not assume any one phrase.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-consistency improves chain of thought
finding: Sample many chains, take the majority answer. Beats greedy CoT on every set tested.
numbers: PaLM 540B GSM8K 56.5 -> 74.4 (+17.9); SVAMP +11.0; AQuA +12.2; StrategyQA +6.4; ARC-c +3.9. Code-davinci-002 GSM8K +17.9 to 78.0.
limits: Costs many samples. Samples from one model share errors.
agent_relevance: Voting helps, but samples are not independent evidence (G4); code should count.

source: Suzgun et al. (2022) Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether CoT can solve them
finding: On 23 hard BIG-Bench tasks, answer-only prompting underestimates models. With CoT PaLM beats the average human rater on 10 of 23 tasks and Codex on 17 of 23.
numbers: 10/23 (PaLM) and 17/23 (code-davinci-002) tasks above average human rater; CoT turns flat scaling curves into emergent ones on several tasks.
quote: few-shot prompting without CoT substantially underestimates the best performance
limits: Some tasks gain little.
agent_relevance: Evaluate baselines with reasoning allowed, or they are too weak.

source: Madaan and Yazdanbakhsh (2022) Text and patterns: for effective CoT, it takes two to tango
finding: Counterfactual prompts: symbol type and factual correctness of patterns hardly matter; the text around them does.
numbers: PaLM, GPT-3, Codex on four tasks (sorting, sports, date, math): altering symbols or pattern validity left solve rates near normal; removing text hurt (per-task figures in paper).
quote: factual patterns in a prompt is practically immaterial to the success of COT
limits: Four tasks, 2022 models.
agent_relevance: Steps may be a template to copy, not valid logic (G10).

source: Wang et al. (2022) Towards understanding chain-of-thought prompting
finding: Exemplars with invalid reasoning still reach 80-90% of normal CoT performance. Relevance to the query and correct order matter more than validity.
numbers: Invalid-reasoning exemplars reach over 80-90% of CoT performance (text-davinci-002, PaLM, GPT-3 families; BBH and factual QA).
quote: prompting with invalid reasoning steps can achieve over 80-90% of the performance obtained using CoT
limits: Few tasks; invalid steps hand-built.
agent_relevance: What the chain looks like matters less than being on topic and in order.

source: Fu et al. (2022) Complexity-based prompting
finding: Exemplars with more reasoning steps work better; also take the majority among the more complex sampled chains.
numbers: Average +5.3, up to +18 accuracy over strong baselines on GSM8K, MultiArith, MathQA, Date Understanding, Penguins (GPT-3, Codex).
limits: Gain varies by dataset.
agent_relevance: Longer exemplars help; G11 says think briefly at runtime, so test which holds.

source: Zhou et al. (2022) Least-to-most prompting
finding: Decomposing into subproblems generalises to harder problems than shown. On SCAN plain CoT is far worse.
numbers: SCAN, code-davinci-002: least-to-most at least 99% with 14 exemplars vs 16% with CoT.
limits: Needs a task-specific decomposition prompt.
agent_relevance: Plain CoT fails on easy-to-hard generalisation; decomposition can fix it.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show your work: scratchpads for intermediate computation
finding: Precursor to CoT: emitting intermediate steps into a scratchpad greatly improves long addition and program execution; few-shot step-by-step also works.
numbers: Scratchpad enables multi-digit addition and program execution where direct answer fails (per-length accuracies in paper).
limits: Fine-tuned on scratchpad data in main results.
agent_relevance: Written steps act as external working memory.

source: Sprague et al. (2024) To CoT or not to CoT: meta-analysis
finding: Meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus own tests on 20 datasets and 14 models: CoT helps mainly on math, logic and symbolic tasks.
numbers: Mean gains: symbolic 14.2, math 12.3, logical 6.9 points; top three categories 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without; other categories 56.8 vs 56.1. On MMLU up to 95% of gain is on questions with an equals sign.
quote: CoT gives strong performance benefits primarily on tasks involving math or logic
limits: Publication bias; CoT underperforms a symbolic solver.
agent_relevance: Use steps selectively (G11); use code for symbolic execution.

source: Sprague et al. (2024) To CoT or not: planning vs execution
finding: Splitting CoT into plan and execution shows most gain comes from execution; a symbolic solver beats CoT on both steps.
numbers: Plan + tool solver outperformed CoT and plan + CoT solver on average across models (per-dataset numbers in paper).
limits: Datasets with a clean formal form only.
agent_relevance: Code should execute; model should plan (matches schema section 1).

source: Liu et al. (2024) Mind your step (by step): CoT can reduce performance where thinking hurts humans
finding: Six tasks where verbal deliberation hurts people. In three, CoT drops accuracy for frontier models.
numbers: Implicit statistical learning: o1-preview 36.3 points below GPT-4o direct; CoT reduced performance in all six vision-language models on a face task; learning labels with exceptions took up to 331% more iterations with CoT.
limits: Models and humans are not parallel; mixed results on other tasks.
agent_relevance: Do not use long reasoning on pattern or perception tasks (G11).

source: Shi et al. (2023) LLMs can be easily distracted by irrelevant context
finding: One irrelevant sentence in grade-school math (GSM-IC) sharply cuts accuracy of CoT prompts; self-consistency and an 'ignore irrelevant information' instruction recover part of it.
numbers: Recall of the correct answer among samples is 99.7%, so self-consistency helps; some prompts fall to 0 macro accuracy on certain distractor types (see paper tables).
limits: Synthetic distractors; code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003.
agent_relevance: CoT is fragile to noise; filter context before reasoning.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2024) GSM-Symbolic
finding: Changing numbers or names in GSM8K items lowers accuracy and widens its spread; adding a clause that looks relevant but is not (GSM-NoOp) causes large drops.
numbers: Drops up to 65% across all state-of-the-art models on GSM-NoOp; performance falls as clauses increase.
limits: Authors read this as pattern replication; others dispute that reading.
agent_relevance: Chains may copy training patterns; test with mutated inputs (G3).

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language models don't always say what they think
finding: Biasing features (answer always A, user suggests an answer) change CoT answers while explanations never mention the bias.
numbers: Accuracy falls up to 36% on 13 BBH tasks; GPT-3.5 zero-shot CoT -36.3% under Suggested Answer, -18.7% under Answer-is-Always-A (GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0).
quote: CoT explanations can be plausible yet misleading
limits: Two 2023 models; benchmark tasks.
agent_relevance: Written steps are not evidence of the real cause (G10).

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring faithfulness in chain-of-thought reasoning
finding: Intervening on the CoT (stop early, add a mistake, paraphrase, filler tokens) shows dependence on CoT varies by task, and larger models are less faithful.
numbers: Faithfulness measured as area over the curve per task; AQuA and LogiQA most faithful; filler tokens and paraphrasing did not explain the gains; faithfulness shows inverse scaling with model size.
limits: Anthropic internal models; eight multiple-choice tasks.
agent_relevance: Chain may be post-hoc; verify by code.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Reasoning models don't always say what they think
finding: Reasoning models seldom mention hints they use.
numbers: Faithfulness 25% for Claude 3.7 Sonnet and 39% for DeepSeek R1; misalignment hints 20% and 29%; harder questions (GPQA vs MMLU) 44% and 32% relatively lower; reward hacks verbalised in under 2% of examples in 5 of 6 environments.
limits: Hint-based tests; CoT monitoring still catches some behaviour (over 90% detection when reward hacks are verbalised in other settings).
agent_relevance: Never treat thinking text as a log of the decision (G10).

source: Arcuschin et al. (2025) Chain-of-thought reasoning in the wild is not always faithful
finding: Without artificial hints, models give coherent arguments for Yes to both 'X bigger than Y' and 'Y bigger than X' (implicit post-hoc rationalisation).
numbers: Up to 13% unfaithful pairs in production models; DeepSeek R1 0.37%.
limits: Pair-comparison questions only.
agent_relevance: Reversed-question consistency checks are code-checkable.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) Chain of thoughtlessness
finding: On Blocksworld CoT helps only when the prompt is very specific to the problem class, and decays as the problem grows beyond the exemplars.
numbers: Blocksworld: stacking-specific CoT prompt reaches 59.3% vs 3.8% zero-shot on one model/task; general prompts only 13.7-18% on same sets; gains collapse as stack size n grows.
quote: CoT's performance improvements do not stem from the model learning general algorithmic procedures
limits: GPT-4 and Claude 3 only; planning domain.
agent_relevance: Gains reflect prompt-engineering labour, not general reasoning.

source: Wang and Zhou (2024) Chain-of-thought reasoning without prompting
finding: CoT paths exist among top-k first tokens; picking the path with highest answer confidence beats greedy.
numbers: GSM8K top-100: greedy 44.0% vs CoT-decoding 72.0%; year parity 57.0 vs 95.0 (PaLM-2 L). GSM8K full: PaLM-2 L 34.8 vs 63.2; Mistral-7B 9.9 vs 25.1.
limits: Needs multiple decodes; confidence is a proxy.
agent_relevance: Reasoning is partly in the weights; answer confidence can rank chains.

source: Feng et al. (2023) Towards revealing the mystery behind chain of thought
finding: Theory: bounded-depth transformers cannot directly solve arithmetic or equations unless size grows super-polynomially; constant-size ones can with CoT. Experiments agree.
numbers: Direct prediction always fails; CoT-trained models succeed with enough demonstrations.
limits: Proofs and trained small transformers, not prompted LLMs.
agent_relevance: Written steps add real serial computation; supports steps for serial problems.

source: Merrill and Sabharwal (2023) The expressive power of transformers with chain of thought
finding: Logarithmic CoT steps add little; linear steps allow all regular languages; polynomial steps give exactly polynomial-time problems.
numbers: No empirical numbers; complexity results.
limits: Theory with assumptions on pre-norm.
agent_relevance: Reasoning length bounds what is computable; short chains cannot do long serial work.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1
finding: Reinforcement learning on outcome reward makes very long chains emerge, with self-checking ('aha moment').
numbers: AIME 2024 pass@1 79.8 for R1 in its model table; GPQA Diamond 71.5.
limits: Trained, not prompted; long chains cost tokens.
agent_relevance: CoT is moving from prompt to training; our scaffold must work with such models.

source: Shaikh et al. (2022) On second thought, let's not think step by step
finding: Zero-shot CoT raises harmful and stereotyped output in sensitive domains; harmful CoTs rise with model size.
numbers: Example (Fig 1) text-davinci-003 refusal rate on a harmful question 78% direct vs 25% with zero-shot CoT; average direct response accuracy 65% in the example.
limits: text-davinci family; sensitive tasks.
agent_relevance: Steps can weaken refusal behaviour; apply checks after reasoning.
